title: Cocquet to Mangot, Rome, 13? November 1616, BnF Clairambault 369 ff. 316-317

plaintext.source: Not in DECODE; Tomokiyo lists it as not deciphered.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF full-resolution image of view 329 (6124 x 5431), own line crops
transcription.notes: transcription_f317.txt (14 Nov 2026): two blind passes by independent agents (188 and 187 cipher tokens), compared sign by sign and arbitrated on 2-4x crops; 186 tokens in 9 cipher-bearing lines, about 45-50 distinct signs; 9 places left as {x|y}.

system.summary: Letter-shaped signs (round d, theta, q, long s, PU, pi, infinity loop, barred t's, $), underlined signs, signs with two dots, and two-digit numbers (86 three times, 89) in short runs inside clear French. Same construction as de Castille's 1616 cipher in the same volume (Tomokiyo's reconstruction, Clair 369 f. 11); not tested as a key.

diacritics.note: Underlined pairs and ö with two dots; function unknown.

system.sibling_key: Lead, not measured: de Castille's cipher (Clair 369 f. 11, Tomokiyo 2016-) has the same build: letter homophones drawn as d, theta, H, eta, q, g, long s, a barred ff, a barred #, pi as a null, two-digit syllable codes in the 73-99 range (85 con, 88 de, 89 di) and digits with two dots for syllables. Cocquet uses 86 (x3) and 89, o with two dots, pi, theta, round d, H, eta, q, g, long s and a barred ff. Baugy and Du Maurier are figure ciphers; the Clair 372/373 anonymous keys use numeric word codes.
system.notes: About 45-50 distinct signs (42 firm labels plus 9 unresolved {x|y} places in transcription_f317.txt; 47 is the midpoint). Repertoire from a labelled two-pass transcription (14 Nov 2026). The 16 Sept 2026 gate note said Castille shares 'only generic shapes'; with the labelled transcription the overlap is structural (same sign classes and the same two-digit syllable band), though the values may differ.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo: not deciphered; no DECODE record

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Located f. 317 as Gallica canvas 329 and fetched full-resolution images.
Gate measurement: about 160 glyphs over 40-50 units in nine runs, the du Croc regime, below threshold.
Compared the repertoire with five period keys from Clair 369, 372, 373.
Searched DECODE for Cocquet, Mangot, Trainel, Clairambault and Tomokiyo's Louis XIII page for siblings.

Labelled transcription of the nine cipher-bearing lines of f. 317: two blind passes by independent agents from the full Gallica image (188 and 187 tokens), compared sign by sign, disagreements settled on crops; 186 tokens, about 45-50 distinct signs, 9 unresolved places marked. transcription_f317.txt.

Compared the labelled repertoire with Tomokiyo's reconstructed Clair 369 keys (Castille f. 11, Baugy f. 109, Du Maurier ff. 229, 294) by sign class. Castille's cipher has the same build (letter-shape homophones, pi null, barred ff, two-digit syllable codes 73-99, digits and letters with two dots); Baugy and Du Maurier do not. Recorded as a lead; Castille's key was not applied and nothing was measured.

Integration check: 74 signs of lines 1-3 compared with the Gallica image (IIIF crops), all present in the transcription; then Tomokiyo's reconstruction of de Castille's 1616 key (Clair 369 f. 11) applied once by shape correspondence (castille_test.py). 108 of 186 tokens have a same-shape sign in Castille's table; B, PU and the infinity loop (the 2nd-4th commonest signs), L, s and $ have none. The mapped part gives f as the commonest letter (from the round d), e 4 times, and no French word. Castille's key as reconstructed does not decipher f. 317; the family lead stays a hypothesis.

outcome.method_basis: About 160 signs in nine short runs on Clairambault 369 f. 317; five period keys from the same volumes did not match, and it was closed at the length gate without an attack.
outcome.notes: Closed at the gate on 16 Sept 2026; a labelled two-pass transcription was added on 14 Nov 2026, and de Castille's 1616 cipher (same volume) is the family lead. Not read. Castille's key applied once on 14 Nov 2026: failed (58% of tokens map, wrong letter frequencies, no French).
